The focus road facet and the 109:1 hidden-pass facet make a specific prepared-route contact. The resulting sheltered passage is a qualified local image, not a replacement for the focus worship act.

The packet supplies articulated speech, its tongue instrument, the named audience's truth-rejection field, the focus devotional act, and the closing religion allocation. Together they change the focus from an isolated contrast into an overtly assigned worship boundary.

The devotional-worship facet is carried by the focus verbs and the 109:1 bowed-submission facet supplies an independent bodily trigger. Their contact adds a posture of allegiance while keeping the ordinary worship reading recoverable.

The focus ship-covering facet and the 109:1 engulfing-vastness facet provide separate material carriers for a sealed vessel moving through water. The packet bounds this as an analogy rather than a literal gloss of the worship verb.

The focus supplies owned-person and enslavement facets, and 109:6 supplies the distinct subjugation-and-possession relation. The branches explain one hierarchy of possessor, possessed person, and compelled service, with an explicit analogy boundary.

The focus root recurs through 109:2-109:5 with changing subject roles and forms, supplying an independent structural trigger for the supplied treated, swift, and resistant-mount facets. The complete carrier arc is retained as a qualified analogy.

The commanded speech in 109:1 supplies circulating and privately drawn talk, the audience label supplies a remote tract, and the focus supplies a stalled or resistant carrier. These contacts make a specific interrupted-transit image rather than a generic movement theme.

The 109:1 public-talk and truth-rejection carriers meet the focus dispersion facets and the 109:6 religious-way carrier. The contact gives doctrinal difference a social and spatial dispersal mechanism beyond the plain denial alone.

The focus devotional-submission facet is independently contacted by the 109:6 obedience carrier and the 109:1 coercion-into-disobedience carrier. The resulting redirected-allegiance scene is bounded as an analogy, not a historical assertion.

The 109:1 expiation carrier supplies a concrete counterpart for both focus timing facets, so the focus contrast can be read through prompt covering and discharge of an offense. The source itself bounds this as a cross-domain analogy.

The focus emotional facets meet the 109:1 supplied doctrine and ascription-of-unbelief carriers. The packet describes a connected movement from naming to protective anger to grief, with each emotional direction retained and bounded.

The exact HFT trace links the commanded utterance in 109:1 to the focus refusal, names vocal production and saying-as-position, and records a changed reading from private difference to accountable public boundary. The legacy-unbound status qualifies the inference but does not suppress it.

findings.title: Crowned voice and honored ruler
findings.claim: The focus refusal can be heard within a local scene of a commanded, crowned authority whose word carries force and whose service is received.
findings.mechanism: The qawl carrier in 109:1 supplies a titled speaking office, the kfr carrier supplies a covering crown image, and the focus service relation supplies the superior who receives honor. Their contact turns the refusal into a stance before an authority while the ordinary worship act remains intact.
findings.reader_payoff: The command, audience label, and worship verb become a visible hierarchy of voice, rank, and received service rather than three disconnected lexical details.
findings.containment: The focus still says that the speaker does not worship what the addressees worship. The ruler scene is a bounded root-level resonance; it does not assert a historical monarch or replace the devotional reading. A plain command with no performative authority remains a live alternative.

epistemic.reason: Exact focus and context occurrences support the contact, while the authority scene is a channel-derived macro inference rather than a local grammatical assertion.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The speaker's refusal stands before an authority whose status is publicly marked and whose service is received.
branch_activations.boundary: This is the honored-person facet only; it does not turn the worship verb into a literal royal title.

findings.title: Prepared road through a sheltered pass
findings.claim: The repeated service relation can locally open as a route made passable through a concealed pass, so the refusal marks whether one enters that route.
findings.mechanism: The focus road facet supplies a surface made usable by repeated passage, while the 109:1 audience occurrence supplies an enclosing or hidden mountain pass. The prepared road and difficult enclosure explain one another as a route scene.
findings.reader_payoff: The worship relation acquires a concrete question of passage: a concealed setting becomes traversable through a prepared surface.
findings.containment: The ordinary focus remains a present-tense refusal to worship the addressees' object field. The road and pass are a bounded analogy, not a surah-wide path claim and not a literal transport meaning of the verb.

epistemic.reason: The two exact root occurrences and trusted channel support form a coherent local contact, but the physical route is an inferred resonance.

branch_activations.boundary: The route is an analogy anchored in the two supplied facets; the focus verb still means worship in its ordinary reading.

findings.title: Public declaration of distinct worship
findings.claim: Within the six-ayah frame, the focus is an overtly spoken partition of worship: an articulated voice, named audience, reciprocal clauses, and separately assigned dīn make the difference social.
findings.mechanism: The imperative speech and tongue carriers in 109:1 bring the focus verb into public articulation; the audience's truth-rejection label, the devotional focus facet, and the closing religion carrier connect that speech to two communities whose worship relations are assigned separately.
findings.reader_payoff: The sentence becomes a performed boundary between parties, not merely an inward report that two people happen to worship differently.
findings.containment: The ordinary content remains the speaker's refusal of the addressees' worship object. The social declaration is a macro reading of the supplied pericope and does not select a single theological interpretation of dīn.

epistemic.reason: Every carrier is directly represented in the supplied pericope and the trusted nomination supplies their relation; the social synthesis remains an inference.

findings.title: Bowed service and devotional allegiance

findings.mechanism: The focus devotional facet meets the bowed-submission image attached to the preceding audience occurrence. The act and posture explain one another as a scene of chosen allegiance.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see worship as an enacted relation of lowering and service, not only as an abstract doctrinal label.
findings.containment: The focus still states the speaker's worship refusal. A physical bow is a contextual image supplied by the packet, not a claim that the verb literally denotes a gesture or that the audience actually bows here.

epistemic.reason: The two supplied branch carriers form a direct cross-root relation, while the bodily scene remains an inferred macro resonance.

findings.title: Chattel hierarchy and coerced labor
findings.claim: The repeated service relation can locally depict a hierarchy in which a person is owned, made subject, and compelled under another's control.
findings.mechanism: The focus owned-person and enslaving facets supply the person and the transition into subjection, while the dīn subjugation-and-possession carrier in 109:6 supplies the controlling jurisdiction. These roles form one hierarchy rather than three unrelated definitions.
findings.reader_payoff: The service vocabulary becomes a complete social mechanism of possessor, possessed person, compulsion, and work.
findings.containment: The ordinary focus remains devotional worship and its object clause. The hierarchy is a bounded image pressure; it does not claim that the ayah is legally describing slavery or that worship literally equals coerced labor.

epistemic.reason: All three supplied facets have exact focus or pericope carriers and the candidate support supplies their connecting mechanism; the social scene remains inferred.

findings.title: Prepared but resistant mount
findings.claim: Across the repeated forms, service can be imagined as a prepared mount that moves swiftly yet may resist handling, so readiness and compliance separate.
findings.mechanism: The focus supplies the treated-camel, swift-running, and resistant-camel facets. The 109:3-109:5 repetitions supply changing subject roles and forms, giving the three physical states a temporal and relational sequence.
findings.reader_payoff: Preparation no longer guarantees obedience: the image distinguishes a carrier made ready from a carrier that actually follows its handler.
findings.containment: The focus still concerns worship in the present. The mount arc is a multi-step root analogy grounded in the repeated pericope pattern, not a claim that the ayat describe an animal or that every available root branch is active.

epistemic.reason: The exact repeated focus-root occurrences and supplied form sequence provide a structural trigger for the three nominated facets, while the mount scene remains a channel-derived analogy.

findings.title: Speech in transit and carrier breakdown
findings.claim: The commanded worship boundary can be pictured as public talk drawn into one speaker's possession and stranded when its carrier fails in a remote tract.
findings.mechanism: The focus resistant-carrier facet supplies the breakdown, while the preceding qawl facets supply talk that circulates and can be pulled into one speaker's possession; the kfr remote-place facet supplies the setting where movement stops.
findings.reader_payoff: The declaration becomes a material transit process: speech has a route, a carrier, a point of appropriation, and a place where circulation breaks.
findings.containment: The focus remains a spoken worship refusal. The transit scene is a bounded analogy and does not claim that the ayah literally describes a journey, a lost mount, or private appropriation of a saying.

epistemic.reason: The supplied qawl, kfr, and focus carriers form a functional scene with an explicit breakdown mechanism, but its material form is analogical.

findings.title: Circulating talk and factional dispersal
findings.claim: The declaration's difference can spread as public talk while the parties disperse into separate groups and religious courses.
findings.mechanism: The qawl public-talk carrier and kfr truth-rejection carrier in 109:1 meet the focus dispersion facets, while the dīn obedience-and-submission carrier in 109:6 gives the separated groups distinct courses of allegiance.
findings.reader_payoff: Doctrinal difference acquires a social geography: speech circulates, groups separate, and each course carries its own order of allegiance.
findings.containment: The focus still asserts the speaker's nonparticipation in the addressees' worship. Dispersal is a pericope-bounded resonance, not a whole-surah thesis or a claim that every party has physically moved.

epistemic.reason: The packet supplies exact carriers in 109:1, 109:2, and 109:6 and a connecting social mechanism; the larger spatial synthesis is inferred.
